newsitem.title: JORDAN: Saudi billionare prince invests in Palestinian firm.
newsitem.headline: Saudi billionare prince invests in Palestinian firm.

text.p: Saudi billionare Prince al-Waleed bin Talal has invested $10 million in the flagship Palestinian PADICO firm, the first foray by a prominent Saudi investor in the nascent Palestinian market, the company said on Monday.

PADICO said Prince al Waleed agreed to join as a shareholder in the Liberian registered $200 million capital Palestine Development and Investment Company (PADICO) which aims to set up projects worth $1 billion in Gaza and the West Bank by 2000.

Officials in the Amman-based regional office of the investment holding company told Reuters the prince's investment heralded the start of wider investments in projects undertaken by PADICO's subsidiaries in the Palestinian market.
"The prince's stake will not be limited to this sum and he has expressed his wish and initial commitment to invest directly in the other projects of the company," the official said.

PADICO, the largest firm operating in Palestinian self-rule areas, is spearheading multimillion dollar private investments spanning telecommunications to real estate, industrial parks and tourism and also manages the Palestinian stock exchange.

The prince will initially examine PADICO's real estate and tourism projects, where the $25 million capital Palestine Tourism Investment Company is already proceeding with a $40 million five-star hotel and commercial complex in Bethlehem. It also plans tourist ventures in Arab East Jerusalem.
The Palestine Real Estate Company is proceeding with the largest housing projects yet in Gaza.

The mega-investor Saudi prince who has established a reputation as a shrewd global investor has an investment empire which embraces banking, property and famous leisure businesses including landmark luxury hotels, tourism and entertainment.
His foray into Palestinian investment follows aggressive purchases elsewhere in the Middle East including banking and tourism sectors in Egypt and Lebanon.

Businessmen say it is also the first by such a high profile Arab investor since Middle East peace accords, which should encourage other wealthy Gulf Arab investors to put money into viable investment projects in the nascent Palestinian economy.
A climate of uncertainty about Middle East peace has made many Palestinian and Arab investors hesitant to embark on any substantial ventures in the territories.

"It's a very important vote of confidence in the Palestinian economy and the peace process. It's not just symbolic and it opens the door for further Arab and foreign investment," said a Jordanian with substantial investment in the West Bank.

PADICO was set up after a 1993 deal on Palestinian self-rule to mobilise expatriate Palestinians for business projects in Gaza and the West Bank. Shareholders include influential Palestinians with business empires in the Gulf and the West.

The investment group says its diversified projects are proceeding despite a difficult investment climate due to stalled Israeli-Palestinian peace talks and Israeli obstacles to free flow of goods and labour to self-rule areas.
